name: SU(2)xU(1)_Y action on the Higgs doublet leaves H^dagger H invariant; -v is gauge-equivalent to +v

source.located: The classic electroweak construction (Glashow 1961, Weinberg 1967, Salam 1968; Higgs/Englert-Brout 1964) is NAMED-NOT-READ (pre-arXiv). Read through two arXiv restatements: (1) A. Maas, 'Brout-Englert-Higgs physics: From foundations to phenomenology', arXiv:1712.04721v4 (2019): eqs. (3), (4) p.2; sec. 1.3 p.2-3; sec. 3.1 eqs. (31)-(34) p.17-18 incl. footnotes 13-14; sec. 3.2 eqs. (35)-(37) p.18-19; sec. 4.7.1 p.63. (2) T. Cohen, N. Craig, X. Lu, D. Sutherland, 'Is SMEFT Enough?', arXiv:2008.08597v2 (2021): eqs. (2.7)-(2.9) p.11, sec. 4.1 eq. (4.1) p.18-19, sec. 4.2 p.25 (the CWZ linearization lemma and the O(4) fixed-point criterion).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1712.04721 (pdf pages 1,2,4-7,20-22,66,101 returned) and on 2008.08597 (pdf pages 1,4-7,11,17-19,23,25,29,30,42,44 returned). The group theory itself (the claim is an identity about a representation of a compact Lie group on C^2) is additionally re-derived symbolically here, which does not depend on any reading.

published_statement: Maas 1712.04721 p.18-19 (sec. 3.2): 'Since the potential is, by construction, a function of gauge-invariant quantities only, so are the minima given by gauge-invariant conditions. I. e., phi^dagger phi = f^2 (35) ... In the standard model case (33), this condition takes the form X = v alpha, with v = f and alpha an arbitrary SU(2) matrix, since alpha^dagger alpha = 1. This also shows that the minimum is manifestly invariant under both, gauge transformations and custodial transformations.' p.19: 'In the standard-model case the Higgs field is in the fundamental representation of SU(2), and the only group-invariant from which an invariant potential could be built is phi^dagger phi.' p.2 (sec. 1.3): 'v, in contrast to the parameter f of the Lagrangian (3), is dependent on the gauge. In fact, it is possible to construct gauges ... in which <phi> = 0 always holds.' p.63 (sec. 4.7.1): 'The Higgs field transforms like phi -> g phi = exp(i alpha(y)) phi under a hypercharge gauge transformation.' Cohen et al. 2008.08597 p.11: H = (1/sqrt2)(phi1 + i phi2, phi3 + i phi4) <=> phi-vec = (v0 + h) n-vec (2.7); 'At zero-derivative order, there is only one O(4)-symmetric building block: |H|^2 = (1/2) phi.phi = (1/2)(v0 + h)^2 (2.8)'.
published_hypotheses: Higgs field in the fundamental (doublet) representation of SU(2)_L, with a U(1)_Y hypercharge phase exp(i alpha Y) (Maas eq. (31)-(33), p.63; Cohen et al. eq. (2.7))
a single Higgs doublet (Maas p.2 'the simplest case ... a complex doublet'; multi-doublet potentials with several minima on different orbits are treated separately, Maas p.18 and sec. 3.9)

the potential is a polynomial (renormalizable) function of gauge-invariant combinations only (Maas p.2, p.18 'For simplicity, only this polynomial case will be considered'); Cohen et al. at zero-derivative order with custodial O(4) assumed (footnote 3, p.4)
classical / tree level: 'the minima' are field configurations; at the quantum level the vev is gauge-dependent (Elitzur; Maas sec. 1.3, 3.6)
the transformation is a (global or local) gauge transformation acting on every charged field simultaneously; a space-time dependent element generates derivative terms (Maas eq. (31) minimal coupling)
space-time dimension >= 3 for the symmetry-breaking statements (Maas p.4, p.17)
hypothesis_drift: ADDED QUALIFIER NEEDED, NOT A REFUTATION (excite.py:181-185): 'Moving along T1, T2, T3 or Y leaves H^dagger H invariant, so no mass and no derivative-free gauge-invariant local observable changes.' As a gauge transformation of ALL fields this is true by definition of gauge invariance. If only H is moved (as the --selftest at excite.py:1578-1586 and --verify V14 at excite.py:1873-1882 do) it holds for (a) every function of H alone -- SU(2) acts transitively on each sphere H^dag H = r^2 (re-derived, S1), and (b) every mass: the gauge-boson mass-matrix characteristic polynomial depends on H only through H^dag H (re-derived, S2); but a MIXED derivative-free invariant such as psi^dag H (the shape of a Yukawa L-bar H e) changes when H alone rotates at fixed psi (re-derived CONTROL S4) and is invariant only when psi rotates with it. The tree's sentence carries no 'of H alone / jointly' qualifier. Its conclusion (flat directions are inert) survives either reading because masses are eigenvalues; the qualifier is a scope note.

UNSTATED, TREE-LEVEL (excite.py:181-185, 1087-1088 FLAT_DIRECTIONS_ARE_INERT): the tree states D19 classically. At the quantum level the source says the vev itself is gauge-dependent and gauges exist with <phi> = 0 (Maas p.2, sec. 3.6, Elitzur); the tree's conclusion is not weakened by this -- if anything the gauge directions are less physical -- but the level at which the statement is made is not named.

NAMED CORRECTLY (excite.py:121-125, 1484-1489): 'in the doublet -v is gauge-equivalent to +v'. The selftest exhibits U = -I via the tree's 'Y' generator and labels it '(U = -1 in U(1)_Y)'; -I is equally the SU(2) centre element exp(i pi sigma3) (re-derived, C2). No drift; recorded because the label names only one of the two subgroups that contain it.

NAMED CORRECTLY: 'the Higgs is an SU(2) doublet with hypercharge' and 'masses depend only on H^dagger H' (canonical hypotheses) match the source; the second is not merely assumed -- it follows from the first at tree level (S1, S2), consistent with Maas p.19 'the only group-invariant ... is phi^dagger phi'.

SINGLE DOUBLET implicit in 'the Higgs is an SU(2) doublet' (excite.py:181-185): with two doublets H1^dag H2 is a derivative-free invariant not a function of H1^dag H1, and moving one doublet relative to the other is physical. excite.py:280-288 lists 'a BSM light scalar' as unanswered, so the tree does not claim beyond one doublet; recorded as a named boundary, not a drift of conclusion.

DISCREPANCY IN THE RESTATING SOURCE, NOT IN THE TREE: Maas 1712.04721 footnote 13 (p.17) says 'in the standard model G = SU(2)/Z2'. Read literally, -I would act trivially and could not map H -> -H. The SM quotient is the diagonal Z6 generated by (e^{2 pi i/3}, -I, e^{2 pi i Y}), which acts trivially on every SM field (re-derived, S3) while -I in SU(2) acts as -1 on H; so the H -> -H element survives any quotient. Recorded as a loose footnote, not repaired, and not quoted as an error in the journal version (not read).

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS 29/29 (output in rederive/sm-higgs-doublet-gauge-structure.out). C1: for T1,T2,T3,Y, cos(th) I + i sin(th) sigma equals the matrix exponential exp(i th sigma), is unitary, and (UH)^dag(UH) - H^dag H = 0 for any real theta and any complex H (also in the physical normalisation exp(i alpha/2)). C2: -I is unitary with det 1, equals exp(i pi sigma3) and exp(2 pi i Y) with Y_H = 1/2, and maps (0, v/sqrt2) to (0, -v/sqrt2). S1: an explicit SU(2) element W(H) takes any H != 0 to (0, sqrt(H^dag H)) (transitivity on each sphere). S2: the characteristic polynomial of M^2_ab = H^dag{t_a,t_b}H equals its value at (0, r), r^2 = H^dag H; eigenvalues at the vev {g^2v^2/4 (x2), (g^2+g'^2)v^2/4, 0}. S3: the Z6 generator acts trivially on Q,u,d,L,e,H; -I in SU(2) acts as -1 on H. S4 CONTROL: psi^dag H is invariant only when psi and H rotate together; it changes when H alone rotates. S5: the four generators span a rank-3 tangent space at the vev (orbit S^3), (Y - T3)/2 moves it and (Y + T3)/2 annihilates it in tree normalisation. Independently, the tree's own excite.py --selftest (D19 rows, DOUBLET row, radial CONTROL) and --verify (V14 T1/T2/T3/Y residuals 0; '0 residual(s) not zero of 44') were run read-only and pass; git status of research/warp-drive unchanged.

later_literature.what: Gauge-invariant (Froehlich-Morchio-Strocchi) formulation: the vev is gauge-dependent (gauges with <phi> = 0 exist), the minimum X = v alpha with arbitrary SU(2) alpha is a whole orbit invariant under gauge and custodial transformations; the physical spectrum is given by gauge-invariant composites. Confirms both claims and places them at tree level.

later_literature.ref: T. Cohen, N. Craig, X. Lu, D. Sutherland, 'Is SMEFT Enough?', arXiv:2008.08597v2 (2021)
later_literature.what: The doublet (SMEFT) description exists iff the scalar manifold has an O(4)-invariant point with analytic metric and potential; HEFT is required when a BSM state gets all its mass from EWSB or there is extra EWSB. Narrows the doublet HYPOTHESIS to an empirical assumption (the tree names it), not D19's conclusion: in either EFT, |H|^2 = (v0+h)^2/2 is the only zero-derivative O(4) building block.
Ongoing programme to discriminate SMEFT from HEFT experimentally (positivity bounds, multi-Higgs amplitudes, di-Higgs). Titles/abstracts only; none bears on the group identity.

lacked_data: The result is an identity about a representation of the compact group SU(2)xU(1) on C^2: H^dag H is invariant under any unitary U, and -I lies in the group. No measured quantity enters it, so no datum the 1960s authors lacked can move it (re-derived here for every angle and every H, 29/29). The only empirical content is the representation assignment -- one doublet with Y = 1/2 -- which the tree names as a hypothesis. What was unknown then and is known now: a 125 GeV scalar exists and behaves as the SM Higgs (the source's context, Maas p.1 refs [8-11]); what is still not settled is whether the scalar sector is linearly realised (SMEFT) or requires HEFT (Cohen et al. 2008.08597, READ). Evidence either way: if HEFT held, the doublet phrasing would need restating but D19's conclusion would not change (h is a gauge singlet; Cohen eq. 2.8); if a second doublet existed, H1^dag H2 would be a physical relative orientation and D19 would not extend to it -- the tree already lists 'a BSM light scalar' as unanswered (excite.py:280-288). M's hypothesis is therefore not supported for this result: nothing lacked changes the conclusion on the hypotheses the tree names.
grade_evidence: Statement READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT in Maas 1712.04721 (p.18-19: minimum is phi^dag phi = f^2, X = v alpha with arbitrary SU(2) alpha, 'manifestly invariant under ... gauge transformations'; p.19: phi^dag phi the only invariant) and Cohen et al. 2008.08597 (eq. 2.8). Symbolic re-derivation agrees for every theta and every complex H (C1), exhibits -I in both SU(2) and U(1)_Y (C2), proves transitivity (S1) and mass-eigenvalue dependence on H^dag H only (S2), and shows the H -> -H element survives the SM Z6 quotient (S3); the tree's own --selftest and --verify pass. No datum enters the conclusion. Scope notes, not narrowings of the conclusion as used: (i) 'no derivative-free gauge-invariant local observable changes' needs 'of H alone, or with all fields transformed jointly' -- a mixed invariant psi^dag H changes if H alone is moved (S4 CONTROL), while every mass is unchanged either way; (ii) the statement is tree level, unnamed in the tree; (iii) single doublet, which the tree names. One discrepancy recorded in the restating review (Maas footnote 13, 'G = SU(2)/Z2') -- a loose footnote, not a refutation of anything, not repaired.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree (or a downstream owner of D19, e.g. specthm SR4) is found to use 'no derivative-free gauge-invariant local observable changes' for a mixed composite (a Yukawa-type psi^dag H) while moving H alone at fixed fermions, or to extend D19 to more than one scalar doublet or to a non-doublet scalar sector; NARROWED also if a quantum-level use of the vev's direction is made without naming the tree-level hypothesis. WRONG only on a group element or an H for which (UH)^dag(UH) != H^dag H with U in the gauge group, which the symbolic check excludes for all four generators and all angles. DATA-DEPENDENT is not reachable: no measured quantity enters.
